passage:
Wednesday night. Three days now. In the corridor on Monday I told Sonali her poem was "kind of childish" in front of everyone. She laughed, but I saw her face. Since then I replay it every night before sleep, word by word, and the same voice says, "How could you be so stupid, idiot, idiot." I skipped the canteen twice to avoid her. I told myself this is what taking it seriously looks like.
But honestly it hasn't fixed anything. All it does is make me want to hide.
Tonight I typed a short message: "Sorry I said that about your poem. It was mean and I didn't mean it." I haven't sent it. I'll send it after breakfast. Maybe I could stop rewinding and just do that.
— Jyoti

qa.q: What did Jyoti say about Sonali's poem?
qa.a: Jyoti said the poem was "kind of childish" in front of everyone.

qa.q: What was Jyoti feeling as the scene replayed each night?
qa.a: Jyoti felt ashamed and embarrassed, calling the self stupid over and over and skipping the canteen to avoid Sonali.

qa.q: What small step could Jyoti take that the replaying has not offered?
qa.a: Jyoti could send the apology message after breakfast. It names the mistake, and it does more than harsh self-review does.

qa.q: How might Sonali have felt when the poem was called childish in front of everyone?
qa.a: Sonali was probably hurt and embarrassed, since she laughed but her face showed something else. She may also have wondered why Jyoti was avoiding her afterwards.

grounding: A teenager replays a harsh remark for days; harsh self-review feels like accountability but mostly produces shame and avoidance.

passage:
Minakshi: I can't stop replaying the assembly thing 😔
Siddharth: the speech?
Minakshi: I forgot the whole second paragraph and just stood there. It's been 4 days and I still hear the silence
Siddharth: honestly I only remember the first line, it was really good
Minakshi: liar
Siddharth: no seriously. Also Dev tripped on the stage steps right after and everybody talked about that 😅
Minakshi: I've been avoiding the staffroom so I don't see Ma'am
Siddharth: what if you just said "that was awkward, I froze" once, out loud? then it's done
Minakshi: ...maybe. tomorrow
Siddharth: I'll walk with you 🙂

qa.q: How many days had it been since the assembly speech?
What was Minakshi feeling about the assembly speech?
qa.a: Minakshi felt embarrassed and ashamed, still hearing the silence and avoiding the staffroom to dodge Ma'am.

qa.q: What could Minakshi do tomorrow to stop the avoiding?
qa.a: Minakshi could tell Ma'am once, out loud, that it was awkward and that Minakshi froze, with Siddharth walking alongside. That would end the hiding.

qa.q: How does Siddharth remember the speech differently from Minakshi?
qa.a: Siddharth remembers the good first line and says that Dev tripping on the steps took over the talk. To Siddharth, the moment was smaller.

grounding: A teenager replays an embarrassing moment for days; harsh review produces shame and avoidance, and a friend offers a way out.
